Cc: procurement@novahealth.com, SRE Team <sre@novahealth.com>

Subject: Request: deferred batch finalization waiver for nightly patient-score jobs

Hi Soojin / Marcus —

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. We drilled into the nightly patient-score job (bulk inference, ~12M records) and ran into a sizing reality: during end-of-month analytics peaks the job frequently runs past the current 01:00 UTC completion window.

We need to request a temporary SLA waiver that:
- expands the job finalization window from 1 hour to up to 3 hours for scheduled nightly runs,
- confirms safe retry semantics (idempotency keys or at-least-once guarantees) so our downstream ETL doesn't double-count, and
- clarifies what credits or remediation Redwood will provide if job completion falls outside the expanded window.

Attached is a short summary and the job schema. Can you confirm whether Redwood can support a 90-day waiver while we optimize sharding/parallelism? If so, we need a signed form for procurement.

Appreciate a quick read — our Q3 production backlog depends on this.

Alex
Alex Morgan
Director, Data Platform | NovaHealth Analytics
Attachments: SLA_waiver_request_v2.pdf, nightly_job_schema.csv
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, procurement@novahealth.com
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: deferred batch finalization waiver for nightly patient-score jobs

Alex —

Thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. We can consider a temporary waiver, but we need to align on three practical guardrails before we sign off:

1) Idempotency and replay behavior- Redwood can accept an idempotency token per job run (client-provided run_id) and will treat duplicate submissions within a configurable dedupe window as no-ops. We recommend a dedupe window of 24 hours for your workload.

2) Completion window and monitoring- We can expand the completion window to 3 hours for a 90-day pilot, provided we maintain active alerts and a per-run completion metric in the Console. Redwood will add a per-run latency tag so you can breakpoint any long tails.

3) Remediation / credits- For the pilot we can offer service credits on missed completions that exceed the 3-hour tolerance on more than 5% of nightly runs in a rolling 14-day window; exact credit language needs procurement/legal review.

Action items:
- Karthik: outline the retry/idempotency semantics and recommended backoff (see Karthik's note below).
- Marcus: add the dashboard tile and an alert rule in Console for "nightly_job_finalization_time".
- Alex / Procurement: sign the attached waiver PDF (we can put it in DocuSign).

I've attached a draft waiver for review. If this looks broadly acceptable I'll loop legal and SRE for final sign-off.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

On Mon, Aug 24, 2026 at 08:34 AM Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Alex —
> 
> Thanks for the clear summary and the attachments.

Thanks — adding technical detail so procurement can be confident the waiver won't create data correctness risk. Summary below:

- Idempotency key: require a stable run_id (UUID) attached to every job submission. Redwood will store a lightweight tombstone per run_id for the configured dedupe window (default 24h). If the same run_id is processed again, the engine will return the original completion status and skip reprocessing models/outputs.

- Checkpointing: for very large jobs we recommend chunked checkpoints (batch_id + offset) and a finalization call (POST /jobs/{run_id}/finalize) that marks a run as complete. Retries can resume from last committed checkpoint; this reduces recompute and avoids partial double-counting.

- Backoff & retries: client should implement exponential backoff for 5xx/timeout responses. Redwood will surface a 409 with existing run metadata for duplicate submissions. For long tail failures we support safe retry up to 3 attempts within the dedupe window; beyond that the client should open a support ticket.

- Observability: we will emit per-chunk processed counters and a final "finalization_latency_seconds" metric. Marcus will add an SLO alert if p95 finalization_time > 1.5 hours.

If procurement/legal want explicit wording about the dedupe tombstone duration we can document it in the waiver.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

This is helpful, thank you. Two quick clarifications from Procurement and SRE:

- Procurement: can you confirm the exact credit formula (we'll need a numeric table for DocuSign)?
- SRE: will the dedupe tombstone be persisted long enough to cover downstream pipeline replays (we typically re-run within 48 hours)?

If Redwood can set the dedupe window to 72 hours for the pilot and provide the credit table, we can route this through DocuSign today. Otherwise we can sign with 24h and reopen if replay needs expand.

I'll wait for Marcus / Soojin's reply so we can finalize procurement routing.

— Alex

Subject: Re: Request: deferred batch finalization waiver for nightly patient-score jobs

Alex —

We can support a 72-hour dedupe tombstone for the 90-day pilot; I'll note that in the waiver draft. Procurement: proposed credit table (draft for DocuSign):

- If missed completion rate >= 5% and < 10% over a 14-day window: 5% invoice credit for that month
- If >= 10% and < 25%: 15% invoice credit for that month
- If >= 25%: escalation to account team + case-by-case remediation (possible larger credit)

Technical notes: Karthik will implement the tombstone persistence option; Marcus will create the finalization SLO tile and a 72-hour dedupe config flag on the account. Legal: I've cc'd legal for any final wording changes.

Next steps:
1) Procurement to confirm which credit row they'll accept.
2) Alex: sign the attached DocuSign waiver after procurement confirms.
3) Redwood to enable 72-hour dedupe flag and add monitoring tile (ETA 48 hours after signature).

Thanks — we'll queue DocuSign once procurement confirms the credit row.

Regards,
